title: Like every budget app, it sucks
text:
Monarch on it’s surface looks great but like every other money app, they focus on features for budgeting long term, but fail to get the month to month right and thus failing to budget forecast correctly. 

One example: Monarch forces your accounts to show statement amounts when sync’d. So for ex: I may have 3 credit cards, one with $1,000, one with $2,000, and one with $3,000 balances. Monarch surfaces this data as “you owe $6,000 this month” and shows the monthly recurring dollar amount as something atrociously high. 

The statement amount and payment amount are not the same thing - the fact that you cant extrapolate that data automatically is one thing. But the fact that I cant MANUALLY set it either makes this app a complete waste of money. $100 a year for an app that can’t get the month to month numbers right is wild.

All of these apps fail to automate something incredibly simple. I end up manually tracking everything anyways with more confusing steps because theres an app in the way. I’ll go back to using my personal Claude app, because it’s free.

title: Great app but can still use a lot of needed features
text:
Love the app but i’m having major problems of not seeing how much i spent on a certain category in the budgeting section which is very annoying.

Even though i don’t have a set budget for a category it would still be helpful to see a quick number on how much i’ve spent on it. Same goes for the “other income” I don’t need to plan something out to understand how much I’ve made in that certain section. 

Example on the flexible tab I have only a couple things budgeted and rest it all depends on the month. The category’s i don’t have a set budget on are left blank leaving me to have to go in and manually check how much spending i’ve done on that category. It’s annoying since i have to go through multiple categories just to see what’s eating up my unallocated budget. 

Wastes a lot of unnecessary time especially when you have over 20 different categories along with spending from multiple people. Until this gets fixed or added i won’t be changing my stars.

title: MUST FIX: Doesn’t support Interest APR% Changes!
text: Forecasting, budgeting and debt paydown functions are all nonfunctional because Monarch does not currently support inputting future changes to credit interest APR % rates. For example- introductory credit or loan offers of 0% for 21 months, that will turn into 20% on a certain date… Monarch only allows inputting the 0% introductory rate, and does not allow to input the future % increase on given date. Therefore retirement forecasting, budgeting and debt paydown functions are not accurate and are useless. This basic oversight totally ruins the app’s promises of multifunctionality and goal tracking. It is only good for tracking transactions & current balances. Monarch admits many users are complaining about this but still hasn’t fixed it. Monarch makes a false promise of a full financial picture but only delivers distorted accounting.  Will update rating if they fix this promptly please!

title: So Close but So Far
text: I have loved monarch but then something works in a way that just makes it absolutely useless for me. One example is I get my card stolen so I get new card. When I sync it it doubles every transaction as they now both count as same card. There is no rule to just skip transactions from one card before or after a certain point. Another is trying to use the rollover budgets for flexible spending. When I turn it off everything is just messed up. The spending in the flexible categories is clearly over the total flexible budget and yet somehow the category is overall under budget? Where did the money go? So now the flexible category is basically useless. I can’t figure out how to do the one thing it says it does which is effectively to use it as a catch all that rolls over for certain categories of spending.
